newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner selects digital suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner selects digital suppliers.

text.p: Time Warner Cable said Tuesday it has selected Scientific-Atlanta Inc as the prime contractor to be the designer and initial supplier of the Digital Video Network on the "Pegasus program."
The Digital Set-tops will be based on standards and an open systems philosophy, the Time Warner Inc unit said.
In addition to Scientific-Atlanta, Time Warner continued, Pioneer Electronic Corp and Toshiba Corp have also been selected to provide digital set-tops.
Time Warner said it expects to buy some one million digital set-tops from these three major electronics companies.
It said Scientific-Atlanta, Toshiba America and Pioneer New Media will make initial deliveries to customers planned in late 1997 and continuing for the next several years.
Time Warner Cable did not disclose the quantity of digital boxes each company would supply, but said the average price per box would be less then $400.
It said Scientific-Atlanta will provide the first digital headend network control systems and digital headend equipment.

General Instrument Corp also has agreed to provide Time Warner Cable with its DCT-1000 digital box so that Time Warner has the option of offering it in cable systems in which it wishes to launch digital services before the Pegasus program rolls out, the company said.
It said General Instrument may also manufacture a second-generation Pegasus box.

As a result of recent standards agreements, it noted, the Pegasus and DCT-1000 digital boxes will comply with the Interoperable Digital Cable Standards, enabling interoperability among the different manufacturers.
"Our experience with the Full Service Network has demonstrated the strong potential of true video on demand," said James A. Chiddix, chief technical officer of Time Warner Cable.

"As a result, the Pegasus digital box also will have the capacity of supporting that business in the future. With as many as a million of these boxes in the field, we will be able to quickly jump-start video on demand when the time is right."

The company said it will use the Pegasus box to offer enhanced, digital pay-per-view channels, new program tiers and an interactive program guide. The box will include MPEG2 video and Dolby AC3 digital audio processing as well as traditional analog broadcast programming.

Future interactive applications will be delivered using a two-way, real time high bandwidth data channel. This will allow customers to use a wireless remote control to access Time Warner's Road Runner and other Internet services, the company said.
